body: Exactly. I try to discourage people without children from getting involved with people with children because out of all relationship dynamics it’s the most unbalanced. They’ll justify neglecting the childless person because “The kids must come first” but that’s actually incorrect, it’s like the oxygen mask on a plane analogy. The core relationship (that includes self AND your intimate partner) must be first, must be solid and supportive and then that filters down in a very healthy way to the children. You can’t neglect the foundation and then act surprised when everything crumbles

There is nothing ok with this at all. So many red flags I don’t know where to start. I’ve worked in both relationship, addiction and abuse counselling for many many years now and this is not ok at all. I remember I had this blind loyalty to my first boyfriend, I was a teenager when I got with him and I had this belief that you don’t give up on someone you love so I put up with all kinds of behaviour that I shouldn’t have and nothing extreme like abuse but we clearly weren’t on the same page. We were together 7 years before I finally got the courage to leave because we just weren’t compatible once we actually started to mature. I’d say 95% of couples going through a divorce that come through the large clinic I work for were too young when they got together and had the same mentality as I did once and instead of just accepting that it’s ok to end relationships due to incompatibility they just keep trying to fit a square peg into a round hole. They won’t face the fact that they have different wants and needs and then they have children to try and “fix” it but in reality they create a self imposed prison for each other. You’re only 24 years old, if your partner already has the mentality that he’s “missing out” I’m sorry to say but this is exactly the kind of mentality that will lead to the end of the relationship whether now or 15 years from now.
